column1: # Rule overrides for the OWASP ZAP baseline scan (ci.yml's zap_baseline job).
# Applies to both of that job's passes, signed-out and signed-in (demo
# mode) -- one file, since the reasoning behind each entry below (a header
# this static export structurally can't send, a content-based check that
# should never fire) doesn't change with the caller's auth state.
# Format: <rule id><TAB><threshold><TAB># <comment>
# Threshold is one of FAIL, WARN, INFO, IGNORE. Anything not listed here
# defaults to WARN and is reported in the scan artifact/job summary but does
# not fail the job -- the workflow passes zap-baseline.py's `-I` flag, so
# only a rule explicitly set to FAIL below can fail this check. See
# TEST_STRATEGY.md's §6 "Dynamic scanning (DAST)" for what this kind of scan
# covers and doesn't, and docs/how-to/developer-guide.md for how to run it
# locally.
# Deliberately short and conservative on a first rollout, per the rule this
# file exists to serve: a false positive here is CI noise nobody asked for,
# so a rule only gets promoted to FAIL once it's both well-established and
# clearly actionable in a static, server-less export. Tighten over time as
# real scan history accumulates -- it can't be guessed from a read-through.
# -- Structurally unfixable on this app's hosting, not just untested --
# GitHub Pages serves static files only; there is no server to send a
# custom HTTP response header from. This app's CSP is a <meta> tag
# (web/src/app/layout.tsx) for exactly that reason, and a <meta> CSP cannot
# carry `frame-ancestors` or `sandbox` -- browsers only honour those from a
# real header -- so the app frame-busts with a same-origin check script
# instead (FRAMEBUST_SCRIPT in layout.tsx). Flagging either rule below would
# be permanent, unfixable noise for an already-documented tradeoff (#334,
# docs/explanation/design-decisions.md).

column3: # X-Frame-Options Header Not Set -- see comment above; mitigated via framebusting script instead
# Content-Security-Policy Header Not Set -- meta CSP only, see comment above

column1: # HSTS is added by GitHub Pages at the edge for HTTPS-enforced hosting, not
# by this app, so it's invisible to a scan of a plain-HTTP local export
# either way. Already tracked as a closed Low-severity finding (#391).

column3: # Strict-Transport-Security Header Not Set -- edge/hosting concern, not app code
